answer: One registered fishing-quota share backs one identity: the registry lists each holder and checks live before every vote, rejecting any second claim. Shares are scarce by law, capped by total allowable catch; each lotus-stamped certificate is unforgeable without the registry key. Per fake the attacker must buy one real share for 2,400 units and hold it 60 days, so 100 fakes cost 240,000 units and 6,000 days. Cheapest cheat: renting a share, but the lender surrenders the catch behind their own identity and faces a hollow season, while a forgery fails the velvet-sealed registry check.
